items.evidence: python roll.py --headless --ticks N --inputs/--script --board --settings-dir prints one JSON object with tick, screen, board, score, lives, ball, coins, crates, bridge_x, volume, language, selected, texts, sounds (e.g. --ticks 5 -> title, selected Start, texts [Roll, Start, Settings, Quit]).
--png after runs on title, settings, paused, won, lost, board 2 and board 3: each file has a PNG signature and IHDR 800 x 480.

sounds/*.wav, also rewritten by python roll.py --wav NAME OUT (output is byte-identical): coin 0.3 s, bounce 0.2 s, fall 0.9 s, clear 0.9 s; RMS 8214/7615/5366/7067; zero crossings 2460/155/749/1701 per s, so all four differ.
Starts on title with Start selected; menu_down -> Settings, menu_down x2 -> Quit, down,down,up -> Settings; 1:enter -> screen play, board 1, score 0, lives 3, ball at (0, ~1.25, 0).

New settings folder: Settings shows Volume: 8, Language: English; menu_right x3 -> 10 (clamped), then menu_left x3 -> 7, menu_left x12 -> 0; menu_right/menu_left on Language toggle es/en; Back + enter -> title.

With es: title [Roll, Empezar, Ajustes, Salir]; settings [Ajustes, Volumen: 8, Idioma: Español, Volver]; play [Tablero 1 de 3, Puntos: 0, Vidas: 3]; paused adds En pausa, Continuar, Salir al título; won [¡Has ganado!, Puntos: 30, Pulsa Intro para volver al título]; lost [Fin del juego, ...]. Only the game name Roll is unchanged.

Volume 10 set in one run, a second run with the same folder shows 10, and a third run lowers it to 7, which is kept; language es was saved to settings.json and later runs start in es (board 3: Tablero 3 de 3). A run with no folder starts at 8, en.
Enter at tick 1, no input: y first <= 0.3 at play tick 26, back above 0.3 at play tick 29 (peaks 0.48, 0.30, 0.26), after 600 play ticks y = 0.25; sounds = 3 x bounce.

First coin: score 0 -> 10, coins 4 -> 3, coin appended. A planned script (judge-scratch/b1.txt) at tick 604: board 2, score 40, ball (-3, 1.25, 0) at rest, the 3 board-2 coins, six crates at x 0, z -0.5/0/0.5, y 0.25/0.75; sounds end coin x4, clear.
--board 2, no input: crates at ticks 1, 60, 150, 300 are within 0.01 of their places (largest drift about 0.008 in z, sag about 0.004 in y).

--board 2 80:right: middle bottom crate goes to x 4.06 and falls off, middle top crate ends at x 0.34 (both > 0.3). Ball reaches x = 1 at tick 185, against 167 with the crates removed; checked every tick: no crate at y < 0.2 while over the board.
Same run: the crate pushed off the edge has y -4.97 before tick 299 and is gone from crates after it (6 -> 5); the other five stay at y about 0.25/0.75.

b1fall script: tick 330 lives 3 ball falling; tick 340 lives 2, sounds +fall, ball (0, 1.247, 0) falling from start at rest; coin stays taken (3 left, score 10). After clearing board 1 the run is on board 2 with lives 2. Board 2 fall: displaced crates are not reset.

judge-scratch/carry.txt (rest on the bridge from tick 616): ball x - bridge_x = -0.034 (600), -0.034 (690), -0.042 (740), -0.048 (780), -0.059 (860), y 0.25, lives 3. A ball pushed right with the bridge away (push 125..140, no brake) falls into the gap at x about -0.7 and loses a life.

judge-scratch/win3.txt with --board 3: tick 928 screen won, score 30, sounds coin x3 + clear; at tick 1100, with right, menu_down and escape sent after the win, the state is identical; 1050:enter -> title.

--board 2 80:right (held): third fall at about tick 696 -> lost, lives 0. The state at tick 700 with no input equals (apart from tick) the state at tick 900 after left, up and escape. 850:enter -> title.

--board 2 escape at 140: paused; ball, crates and score identical at ticks 150 and 400 (left push ignored). --board 3 escape at 100: bridge_x stays 1.111 at 420; escape again or enter on Resume -> play; menu_down + enter -> title.
Two runs: --ticks 400 --board 2 --inputs 80:right,200:up print byte-identical JSON, including crates after the strike (e.g. x 3.23813, 0.340585).

f_b2.png (tick 175): trapezoid board seen from above/in front, red ball with highlight between the crate stack at x 0 and the pushed crate at x 1.1, crates as boxes with lighter top and darker front faces, 3 coins shown. f_b3.png: two green slabs, a gap, and the brown bridge spanning about -0.33 to 1.67 for bridge_x 0.667.

Spanish frames for title, settings, paused, won and lost show the Spanish texts; the English title frame shows Start/Settings/Quit; the play HUD shows Board 2 of 3 / Score / Lives (and Tablero 2 de 3 / Puntos / Vidas). Small flaw: the settings hint '< >' is drawn as '? ?'.

sound.play returns at volume 0 and wav_bytes scales the amplitude by volume/10, and sounds is still listed at volume 0. But play calls winsound.PlaySound(bytes, SND_MEMORY|SND_ASYNC), which on this Python (3.13) raises 'RuntimeError: Cannot play asynchronously from memory' (tested with silent bytes). The error is swallowed, so the game plays no sound at any volume and the volume scaling never reaches the player.
README gives keys and goals, exact commands for the headless run, frame and WAVs (all worked as written), and a per-file description of game.py, render.py, font.py, sound.py, roll.py and selftest.py.

defects: Windowed game is silent: sound.play uses SND_MEMORY|SND_ASYNC, which winsound rejects with a RuntimeError that the game swallows, so no sound is ever heard.

The ball can fall through a slab: landing is only tested when the previous y was >= 0.25, so a ball that dips even one tick over the small gap between the bridge edge and slab 2 then passes through the slab top (seen at x 3.2..3.6, y 0.17 -> -0.17). This makes crossing to board 3's second slab need frame-exact timing (1 of 40 start ticks tried worked).
Ball landing on the bridge takes the bridge's velocity for free (velocity is not converted to the bridge frame when it lands).
The settings screen hint '< >' draws as '? ?' because the bitmap font has no glyphs for < and >.
Coins on board 2 are drawn in a dark brown close to the crate colour, so they are hard to see.
